temperature, different time: thickness decides how long the heat takes to reach the middle. Portion Air fryer Oven reheat Thin-crust slice 350°F / 175°C · 3 min 375°F / 190°C · 8 min Regular slice 350°F / 175°C · 4 min 375°F / 190°C · 10 min Deep-dish or thick pan slice 350°F / 175°C · 6 min 375°F / 190°C · 15 min Why the base stays soft while the cheese overcooks A slice straight from the fridge is cold all the way through, and in an air fryer the heat arrives from above. The cheese and toppings sit right in that stream, so they melt, then sweat oil, then go leathery, while the crust underneath is still cool and a little damp from a night in the box. Turning the dial up only widens that gap. The fix is a moderate temperature and a short time, so heat has a chance to travel down through the slice and drive the moisture out of the base before the top overcooks. Put slices directly on the basket, not on foil, so air reaches the underside, and never stack them: a second slice on top steams the first. Worked example: two regular slices Two slices of a regular takeaway pizza, straight from the fridge. Preheat 4 minutes, lay them side by side on the basket and heat at 350°F for 4 minutes. A thin-crust slice is ready in about 3, and a deep-dish slice needs about 6, because the thick base takes longer to warm through. Reheating a whole tray in a conventional oven instead takes 375°F for around 10 minutes. How to tell it is ready Lift a slice with tongs: it should hold out flat without drooping at the tip, and the underside should look dry and lightly toasted. The cheese should be melted and glossy, just starting to bubble at the edges. If the cheese is browning in patches while the base still bends, the setting was too hot or the slice too thick for the time. Before it goes in Take the slices out of the box a few minutes early so the worst of the chill goes. Pick off and set aside fresh toppings like rocket or basil and add them back afterwards. For a very dry slice, a few drops of water on the basket beside it, not on it, keeps the cheese soft. Related presets Frozen pizza 380°F · 9 min Leftover fries 375°F · 4 min · shake ×1 Leftover fried chicken 375°F · 8 min · flip at 4 375°F oven to air fryer, every food → Oven to air fryer converter → All food presets → Printable conversion chart → Frequently asked questions How long do you reheat pizza in the air fryer? About 4 minutes at 350°F for a regular slice. Thin crust takes around 3 minutes and deep-dish around 6. Why not reheat pizza at a higher temperature? The heat comes from above, so a hotter setting overcooks the cheese before the cold base has warmed and dried out. Should I put foil or parchment under the slice? No. Air needs to reach the underside to crisp it. Only use a liner for very cheesy slices that drip, and keep it smaller than the slice. Is this the same as cooking a frozen pizza? No. A frozen pizza starts raw on top and frozen solid, so it needs a different setting; this one only warms and re-crisps a cooked slice. How do I reheat pizza in the oven? Put the slices on a tray at 375°F for around 10 minutes, or on a preheated tray if you want a crisper base.
